description: pkix-path/src/lib.rs:check_inputs uses chain[i].tbs_certificate.subject_public_key_info == chain[j].tbs_certificate.subject_public_key_info (structural equality via PartialEq) for duplicate detection. This is correct only if the derived PartialEq on SubjectPublicKeyInfoOwned does byte-level comparison. But spki::SubjectPublicKeyInfoOwned derives PartialEq which compares all fields including AlgorithmIdentifier parameters (NULL vs absent) — so two certs with the same key but differing NULL/absent parameter encoding would NOT be flagged as duplicates. The path-builder cycle detection uses spki_der_bytes (actual DER encoding) which would also treat them as different nodes. These are consistent with each other, but both differ from the spki_key_matches function (which compares OID + key bytes, ignoring parameters). Inconsistency is confusing and one of the three approaches is probably wrong for the security goal.
title: duplicate cert detection uses structural equality not SPKI bytes
